verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. At true 800-px web size, and in the 480 side by side, the v4 ball reads as a lighter tomato/coral red against the studio's deep red and v2's darker brick red. It is a uniform lift, not a caustic pattern (upper-half L* p10/p90 46.7/49.6). v2 and v4 share the room and AgX, so the transform does not explain the +8 L*. Round 2 already noted v2 as 'a shade paler and more tomato'; v4 goes further the same way. On the body the ball now sits about 11 L* above its base face (studio about 6). Under the deep-color rule this misstates Ember, so I keep it blocking. Corrections to how the finding is stated: (1) The hue has not turned toward orange. Reflection-free body hue is 37-38 in v4 against 39-40 in the studio. The studio disc's lower hue (35) comes from its pink softbox highlights and floor reflection. The 'tomato' read is +8 to +11 L* plus 16-19 less C*, a paler red, and the C* deficit was already in v2 (AgX). verdicts.reasoning: The band is real and inside the base. But it behaves as the satin (bead-blasted) skin should under this light. Its chroma falls toward the outline on the same curve the studio Core's flanks follow at equal millimetres. It appears only on the side facing the window. Its lilac cast matches the bluish daylight seen in the frame's other dielectric reflections. It is lighter than the studio's flanks because it faces a bright window, not dark studio surroundings. The expected fix (C* above 25 within 6 px of the outline, warm sheen) contradicts the studio reference itself and the frame's lighting. 'Neither has improved' is wrong for the flank: the outer band and every depth on rows 1356-1368 are redder than v2. Only the small shoulder patch went slightly grayer (C* 10.1 to 6.2), and it is as bright as the table's own window sheen beside it (L* 72-74). At 800 px the upper right reads as a soft window sheen on frosted red. v2's dark smoky flanks, the thing the owner asked about, are gone. Worth knowing as a lighting choice: a flag or darker bounce on the window side would warm and darken it. It is not a material or model fault.
